note.note:
Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
- 23-year-old woman with 2-day mid-lower abdominal pain, urinary frequency, and pink-tinged urine; clinical impression is acute uncomplicated cystitis.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Constant mid-lower abdominal (“lower tummy”) pain for 2 days.  
• Associated symptoms: Mild nausea (no vomiting), feels hot/sweaty (home T 37 °C), ↑ urinary frequency, slight pink urine (gross hematuria).  
• Pertinent negatives: No dysuria, flank/back pain, fever >37 °C, vomiting, diarrhoea, upper-abdominal pain/reflux, vaginal discharge, intermenstrual or post-coital bleeding, travel, prior similar episodes.  
• Bowel: Constipated last week, now normal; last BM 2 h ago, normal, no blood.  
• Past medical history: None significant.  
• Allergies: Amoxicillin.  
• Medications: None; previously had contraceptive implant removed 1 y ago.  
• Social: Lives with parents; non-smoker; alcohol ~1 beer on 4 days/week; no recent travel.  
• Family history: Mother—early breast cancer.

Examination:
• No clinician-performed exam (video consult).  
• Patient-reported vitals: Temp 37 °C one hour prior.  
• No flank tenderness or back pain reported.

Impression:
• Most likely: Acute uncomplicated cystitis (suprapubic pain, frequency, visible hematuria, minimal systemic features).  
• Alternate considerations:  
  – Distal ureteric/bladder calculus (hematuria + abdominal discomfort, but pain mild, no colic).  
  – Early appendicitis (central pain, nausea), low likelihood given urinary findings and stable course.

Plan:
• Start 3-day oral antibiotic course (twice daily) sent to patient’s nominated pharmacy (choice not specified; must avoid amoxicillin due to allergy).  
• Symptom-monitoring advice: If worsening pain, fever, back/flank pain, new symptoms, or recurrence, contact service urgently for face-to-face review.  
• Safety-net: Seek care if unable to keep fluids down, hematuria increases, or no improvement after completion of antibiotics.  
• No additional tests arranged during call.

Quality checks:

● Missing/expected elements: Pregnancy status and test not addressed; urine dipstick/culture and full vital signs not obtained; exact antibiotic name/dose unspecified; follow-up timeframe not defined.  
● Transcript/DDx conflicts: None significant (both support UTI).  
● Transcript quality: Generally clear but some audio gaps; limited physical exam and objective data.
